newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Malan says 96 trade gap above $5.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan says 96 trade gap above $5.0 bln.

text.p: Brazil's trade deficit in 1996 was "a little above $5.0 billion", Finance Minister Pedro Malan told state-run Radio Nacional on Wednesday.
Malan said in an interview with the broadcaster that the trade gap in 1997 could be "a little higher than that".

He stressed Brasilia was taking steps to boost exports and improve the trade balance, which has evolved from a $10 billion surplus in 1994 to a $3.157 billion deficit in 1995 and last year's projected $5.0 billion-plus gap.
"We are convinced that Brazilian exports will react to measures the government has been adopting over the past months," Malan said.

He cited the revival of an export insurance agency, plans to introduce new export financing mechanisms and tax exemption for exports of primary and semimanufactured products, which would benefit agricultural sales in particular after the harvest starts in March.
"These will have an effect on exports in 1997, 1998 and beyond," Malan said.
Malan said he was not concerned about high imports.
He pointed out that all great exporting nations were also large importers.
"There isn't one country in the world that isn't a large exporter without at the same time being a large importer," he said.
